gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
gaps.explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

gaps.sentence: 'Where are you going?' she asked her brother. She asked her brother where he ___ going.
gaps.explanation: are you going → he was going: statement order with backshifted continuous.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the thermostat,' the technician warned us. The technician warned us ___ the thermostat.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands are reported with 'warned + object + not to + infinitive'.

gaps.sentence: "It was your fault." — They blamed me ___ the accident.
'Have you ever been to Iceland?' she asked. She asked ___ ever been to Iceland.
gaps.explanation: Have you been → if I had been: if/whether with past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.
